01 / System overview

A small environment to operate.

I use this two-machine lab to run services, experiment with Linux and networking, and operate real workloads.

Debian server
Compute-heavy / server workloads
Raspberry Pi
Lightweight network services / DNS
Administration
SSH / CPU and memory checks

02 / Interactive architecture

One network. Separate roles.

Select a node to explore its role.

  1. Internet

    External connectivity for the home network.

  2. Bell Giga Hub

    The gateway between the Internet and the home network.

  3. Home Network

    Local connectivity shared by both machines and home clients.

  • Debian ServerDebian 12 / Compute & server workloads

    Runs Prominence II. Managed over SSH with CPU, memory, and process monitoring in htop.

  • Raspberry PiRaspberry Pi 4 / Pi-hole & local DNS

    Handles DNS queries and domain filtering. Administered over SSH, separately from the server.

Why this setup? Compute-heavy workloads stay on Debian; lightweight network services stay on the Raspberry Pi.

Technical detail

DNS resolution and service reachability are separate checks. Resolving a name does not confirm that the service itself is reachable.

03 / Hardware explorer

The hardware behind the services.

Drag or use arrow keys to rotate.
Scroll/pinch or use controls to zoom.

Why this hardware? I repurposed existing devices instead of buying dedicated server equipment.

04 / Operations

Running the lab.

Linux administration

SSH, service/process management, and CPU/memory checks with htop.

Technical detail

Process-level readings in htop help distinguish a busy server process from overall host pressure. These are live checks rather than historical monitoring.

Real workload — Prominence II

A demanding multiplayer server provides practice with memory allocation, CPU/resource management, server processes, and connectivity.

Why this workload? A multiplayer server makes resource usage and service behavior observable.

Technical detail

playit.gg provides player connectivity to the Prominence II server. The operations capture shows the tunnel client alongside the running workload.

Network services — Pi-hole

The Pi-hole dashboard shows DNS queries, filtering, blocklists, and client activity on the home network.

Why a separate Pi? DNS stays independent from heavier workloads on the main server.

Technical detail

Filtering happens at the DNS/domain level. Blocked-query information helps distinguish filtering from other connectivity problems.

Privacy: Public screenshots and 3D model textures have private network and user information redacted.

About

Hey, I'm Tim — a backend developer who enjoys building systems that solve real problems.

I have production experience with C#, ASP.NET, SQL Server, and Azure, along with backend development using Node.js and PostgreSQL. I currently work in enterprise IT at DART Aerospace.

When I have free time, I read books, listen to Hans Zimmer, build Python web apps, experimenting with APIs and automation, and trying new ideas that turn my problems into a project. I'm the kind of guy who genuinely enjoys learning and improving with every project. Also, I enjoy solving people's problems, so if you have any, feel free to reach out!
